units.en: Tan had once served under Li Qi and submitted a statement: "Prince Huai'an Li Shentong earned merit in the founding struggle.
units.literal: Tan had once served Li Qi as aide, and therefore submitted a statement saying: "Prince Huai'an Li Shentong had merit in the founding struggle.

units.zh: 且古之父子兄弟，罪不相及，況以锜故累五代祖乎？」
units.en: In antiquity fathers and sons, brothers and brothers did not suffer for one another's crimes. How much less should a fifth-generation ancestor be punished because of Qi?"
units.literal: Moreover, in antiquity father and son, elder and younger brother—punishment did not extend to one another; how much less should the fifth-generation ancestor be implicated because of Qi?"

units.zh: 乃不毀。
units.en: The request was denied.
units.literal: The request was therefore not carried out.

units.zh: 因賜神通墓五戶，以備灑掃。
units.en: Five households were granted to maintain Shentong's tomb.
units.literal: Thereupon five households were granted to Shentong's tomb for sweeping and maintenance.

units.zh: 及武元衡為宰相，以坦為中丞，李元素為大夫，命坦分司東都，未幾歸臺。
units.en: When Wu Yuanheng became chancellor, Tan was made vice censor-in-chief under chief censor Li Yuansu. Tan was posted separately to the eastern capital and soon returned to the Censorate.
units.literal: When Wu Yuanheng became chancellor, Tan was made vice censor-in-chief and Li Yuansu chief censor; Tan was ordered to serve separately at the eastern capital, and before long returned to the Censorate.

units.zh: 裴均為僕射，在班逾位，坦請退之，均不受。
units.en: Pei Jun was Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and stood out of rank in court assembly. Tan asked him to withdraw, but Jun refused.
units.literal: Pei Jun was Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and in court rank exceeded his proper place; Tan requested that he withdraw, but Jun did not accept.

units.zh: 坦曰：「姚南仲為僕射，例如此。」
units.en: Tan said: "When Yao Nanzhong was Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, the precedent was the same."
units.literal: Tan said: "When Yao Nanzhong was Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, the precedent was thus."

units.zh: 均曰：「南仲何人？」
units.en: Jun said: "Who was Nanzhong?"
units.literal: Jun said: "Who was Nanzhong?"

units.zh: 坦曰：「南仲是守正而不交權幸者也。」
units.en: Tan said: "Nanzhong was a man who upheld rectitude and kept clear of the powerful and favored."
units.literal: Tan said: "Nanzhong was one who upheld rectitude and did not consort with the powerful and favored."

units.zh: 尋罷為右庶子，時人歸咎於均。
units.en: Soon afterward Tan was demoted to Right Subvisor. Contemporaries blamed Jun.
units.literal: Soon afterward he was removed and made Right Subvisor; contemporaries blamed Jun.

units.zh: 旬月，出為宣歙池觀察使。
units.en: Within a month he was sent out as observation commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi.
units.literal: Within a month he was sent out as Xuancheng-She-Chi observation commissioner.

units.zh: 三年，入為刑部侍郎、鹽鐵轉運使，改戶部侍郎、判度支。
units.en: In year 3 he entered court as Vice Minister of Justice and Salt and Iron transport commissioner, then became Vice Minister of Revenue overseeing the Revenue Office.
units.literal: In the third year he entered court as Vice Minister of Justice and Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner, then changed to Vice Minister of Revenue and overseer of the Revenue Office.

units.zh: 元和八年，西受降城為河徙浸毀，宰相李吉甫請移兵於天德故城。
units.en: In Yuanhe 8 Western Shouxiang City was damaged when the river shifted. Chancellor Li Jifu proposed moving the garrison to old Tiede City.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanhe, Western Shouxiang City was damaged by a shifting river; Chancellor Li Jifu requested moving the garrison to the old Tiede City.

units.zh: 坦與李絳葉議，以為：「西城張仁願所築，制匈奴上策。
units.en: Tan and Li Jiang jointly argued: "The western city Zhang Renyuan built is the best strategy for holding the northern frontier.
units.literal: Tan and Li Jiang jointly deliberated and considered: "The western city built by Zhang Renyuan is the supreme strategy for controlling the northern nomads.

units.zh: 城當磧口，居虜要沖，美水豐草，邊防所利。
units.en: It sits at the desert pass on the enemy's vital route, with fine water and lush grass—an ideal border fortress.
units.literal: The city sits at the desert pass, occupies the enemy's vital crossing, has fine water and lush grass, and is advantageous for border defense.

units.zh: 今河流之決，不過退就二三里，奈何舍萬代安永之策，徇一時省費之謀？
units.en: The river breach requires retreating only two or three li. Why abandon a plan secure for ten thousand generations for a moment's savings?
units.literal: Now the river's breach requires retreating only two or three li—how can one abandon a plan secure for ten thousand generations and follow a scheme to save costs for a moment?

units.zh: 況天德故城僻處確瘠，其北枕山，與河絕遠，烽候警備，不相統接。
units.en: Moreover old Tiede City lies remote on stony barren ground. Mountains press close to the north, it is far from the river, and its beacon posts do not connect with the rest of the border defense.
units.literal: Moreover the old Tiede City lies remote in stony barrenness; to its north mountains press close, it is utterly far from the river, and beacon posts and watch stations do not connect in unified defense.

units.zh: 虜之唐突，勢無由知，是無故而蹙國二百里，非所利也。」
units.en: Nomad raids would go undetected. This would shrink the border two hundred li for no good reason."
units.literal: When the barbarians raid, there is no way to know—this would without cause shrink the realm by two hundred li; it is not advantageous."

units.zh: 及城使周懷義奏利害，與坦議同。
units.en: Fort commissioner Zhou Huaiyi submitted his analysis, which agreed with Tan's view.
units.literal: When fort commissioner Zhou Huaiyi submitted on advantages and disadvantages, his view agreed with Tan's deliberation.

units.zh: 事竟不行。
units.en: The plan was not carried out.
units.literal: The plan ultimately was not carried out.

units.zh: 未幾，出為劍南東川節度使。
units.en: Before long he was sent out as military commissioner of eastern Sichuan.
units.literal: Before long he was sent out as military commissioner of eastern Sichuan in Jiannan.

units.zh: 在鎮累年，後請收閏月軍吏糧料，以助軍行營，人多非之。
units.en: He held his command many years. Later he requested collection of intercalary-month grain rations for army clerks to support field camps, and many criticized him.
units.literal: He remained at his command many years; later he requested collection of intercalary-month grain rations for army clerks to aid field camps, and many criticized him.

units.zh: 貞元十二年九月卒，年六十九，贈禮部尚書。
units.en: He died in the ninth month of Zhenyuan 12 at sixty-nine and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
units.literal: In the ninth month of the twelfth year of Zhenyuan he died at age sixty-nine and was posthumously awarded Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 史臣曰：古之諍臣，有死於言者。
units.en: The historian writes: Among remonstrating ministers of old, some died for their words.
units.literal: The historian says: Among remonstrating ministers of old, some died for their words.

units.zh: 其次，引裾折檻，不改其操，亦難矣哉！
units.en: Next came those who seized the emperor's robe and broke the balustrade without changing their principles—equally hard!
units.literal: Next to them, those who seized the robe and broke the balustrade without changing their principles—how difficult that also was!

units.zh: 袁高之執盧杞，存誠之戮鑒虛，有古人之遺風焉！
units.en: Yuan Gao's stand against Lu Qi and Cuncheng's execution of Jianxu carry the spirit of the ancients!
units.literal: Yuan Gao's holding Lu Qi, Cuncheng's executing Jianxu—there is the lingering style of the ancients!

units.zh: 平仲觸鱗之氣，糾其謬歟？
units.en: Did Pingzhong's bold remonstrance aim to correct their errors?
units.literal: Pingzhong's spirit of touching the dragon's scales—was it to correct their error?

units.zh: 文洽奪章，以攄府憤；
units.en: Wenqia seized the memorial to vent the army's rage;
units.literal: Wenqia seized the memorial to vent the army headquarters' resentment;

units.zh: 永夷絕食，不飲盜泉，節義之士也。
units.en: Yongyi fasted to death rather than drink from Robber Spring. He was a man of integrity.
units.literal: Yongyi fasted to death and would not drink from Robber Spring—a man of integrity and righteousness.

units.zh: 南仲非葬之言，盧坦西城之議，量之深也。
units.en: Nanzhong's remonstrance against the improper burial and Tan's argument for the western fort show deep judgment.
units.literal: Nanzhong's words against the improper burial and Tan's argument for the western fort show deep measure.

units.zh: 如數子，道為時無君子，乃是厚誣。
units.en: To say that an age with men like these had no gentlemen is gross slander.
units.literal: For men like these to say the age had no gentlemen is gross slander.

units.zh: 贊曰：靈草指佞，諫臣匡失。
units.en: Eulogy: Spirit grass points at flatterers; remonstrating ministers correct the court's errors.
units.literal: Eulogy: Spirit grass points at flatterers; remonstrating ministers correct errors.

units.zh: 惟袁與薛，人中屈軼。
units.en: Among men, only Yuan and Xue are Qu Yi.
units.literal: Only Yuan and Xue among men are Qu Yi.

units.zh: 寬夫雀躍，廷老鴻軒。
units.en: Kuanfu capers like a sparrow; Tinglao struts like a wild goose.
units.literal: Kuanfu leaps like a sparrow; Tinglao soars like a wild goose.

units.zh: 姚、盧啟奏，君子之言。
units.en: The memorials of Yao and Lu are the words of gentlemen.
units.literal: Yao and Lu opened memorials—the words of gentlemen.

units.zh: 元和初，王師討劉辟，郵傳多事，上特令中官為館驛使。
units.en: At the start of Yuanhe, when the imperial army campaigned against Liu Pi, postal affairs multiplied. The emperor specially ordered inner attendants to serve as post-station commissioners.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, when the imperial army campaigned against Liu Pi, postal relay affairs were numerous; the emperor specially ordered inner attendants to serve as post-station commissioners.

units.zh: 尚書敬顯儁曰：「孔子云：『微管仲，吾其被發左衽矣』以此言之，右衽為是。」
units.en: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."
units.literal: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."

units.zh: 薛存誠，字資明，河東人。
units.en: Xue Cuncheng, courtesy name Ziming, came from Hedong.
units.literal: Xue Cuncheng, courtesy name Ziming, was a native of Hedong.

units.zh: 存誠進士擢第，累辟使府，入朝為監察御史，知館驛。
units.en: Cuncheng passed the jinshi examination, served repeatedly on commissioner staffs, entered court as Investigating Censor, and supervised the post stations.
units.literal: Cuncheng passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly summoned to commissioner staffs; he entered court as Investigating Censor and supervised post stations.

units.zh: 上聞甚悅，命中使嘉慰之，由是擢拜御史中丞。
units.en: The emperor was greatly pleased when he heard, sent an inner envoy to praise and comfort him, and promoted him to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: When the emperor heard he was greatly pleased, ordered an inner envoy to praise and comfort him, and thereby promoted him to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 存誠案鞫得奸贓數十萬，獄成，當大辟。
units.en: Cuncheng's investigation uncovered corrupt bribes worth several hundred thousand. When the case was complete, the sentence was death.
units.literal: Cuncheng investigated and interrogated, obtaining evidence of corrupt bribes totaling several hundred thousand; when the case was complete, the sentence was death.

units.zh: 父勝，能文，嘗作《拔河賦》，詞致瀏亮，為時所稱。
units.en: His father Sheng was a skilled writer who once composed the Tug-of-War Rhapsody; its language was fluent and bright, and he was praised by contemporaries.
units.literal: His father Sheng was skilled at writing; he once composed the "Tug-of-War Rhapsody," its wording fluent and bright, and was praised by his contemporaries.

units.zh: 存誠密表論奏，以為有傷公體。
units.en: Cuncheng secretly submitted a memorial arguing that this injured public propriety.
units.literal: Cuncheng secretly submitted a memorial arguing that this harmed public propriety.

units.zh: 會諫官亦論奏，上乃罷之。
units.en: Remonstrating officials submitted memorials as well, and the emperor then abolished the practice.
units.literal: As it happened remonstrating officials also submitted memorials, and the emperor then abolished the practice.

units.zh: 轉殿中侍御史，遷度支員外郎。
units.en: He became Palace Censor and was promoted to vice director of the Revenue Office.
units.literal: He was transferred to Palace Censor and promoted to vice director of the Revenue Office.

units.zh: 裴垍作相，用為起居郎，轉司勛員外、刑部郎中、兼侍御史、知雜事，改兵部郎中、給事中。
units.en: When Pei Ji became chancellor, he was appointed Diarist. He rose to vice director of Merits, director in the Ministry of Justice, concurrent Serving Censor supervising miscellaneous matters, then became director in the Ministry of War and Drafting Attendant.
units.literal: When Pei Ji became chancellor, he was used as Diarist; he was transferred to vice director of Merits, director in the Ministry of Justice, concurrently Serving Censor and supervisor of miscellaneous matters, then changed to director in the Ministry of War and Drafting Attendant.

units.zh: 瓊林庫使奏占工徒太廣，存誠以為此皆奸人竄名，以避征役，不可許。
units.en: The Qionlin Treasury commissioner reported that registered artisans and laborers had grown too numerous. Cuncheng argued that scoundrels were slipping in names to avoid corvée and conscription, and the practice should not be allowed.
units.literal: The Qionlin Treasury commissioner reported that registered artisans and laborers were too numerous; Cuncheng considered that these were all scoundrels who slipped in names to avoid corvée and conscription, and should not be permitted.

units.zh: 咸陽縣尉袁儋與軍鎮相競，軍人無理，遂肆侵誣，儋反受罰。
units.en: Xianyang county defender Yuan Dan clashed with a military garrison. The soldiers acted without cause, slandered him freely, and Dan was punished instead.
units.literal: Xianyang county defender Yuan Dan disputed with a military garrison; the soldiers were without reason, then wantonly slandered and accused him, and Dan in turn was punished.

units.zh: 二敕繼至，存誠皆執之。
units.en: Two edicts arrived in succession, and Cuncheng resisted both.
units.literal: Two edicts arrived in succession, and Cuncheng held to his position on both.

units.zh: 會於頔、杜黃裳家私事發，連逮鑒虛下獄。
units.en: When private scandals at the homes of Yu Di and Du Huangshang came to light, Jianxu was implicated and imprisoned.
units.literal: When private affairs at the homes of Yu Di and Du Huangshang came to light, Jianxu was implicated and imprisoned.

units.zh: 中外權要，更於上前保救，上宣令釋放，存誠不奉詔。
units.en: Powerful figures inside and outside court repeatedly interceded before the emperor. The emperor ordered Jianxu released, but Cuncheng refused to obey.
units.literal: Powerful figures inside and outside court repeatedly interceded before the emperor to save him; the emperor proclaimed an order to release him, but Cuncheng did not obey the edict.

units.zh: 存誠附中使奏曰：「鑒虛罪款已具，陛下若召而赦之，請先殺臣，然後可取。
units.en: Cuncheng sent a report through the inner envoy: "Jianxu's crimes are fully established. If Your Majesty summons and pardons him, kill me first—then you may take him.
units.literal: Cuncheng appended to the inner envoy's report: "Jianxu's crimes are fully established. If Your Majesty summons and pardons him, please kill me first—then you may take him.

units.zh: 不然，臣期不奉詔。」
units.en: Otherwise I will not obey the edict."
units.literal: Otherwise, this subject will surely not obey the edict."

units.zh: 上嘉其有守，從之，鑒虛竟笞死。
units.en: The emperor praised his steadfastness and agreed. Jianxu was beaten to death in the end.
units.literal: The emperor praised his steadfastness and assented; Jianxu was ultimately beaten to death.

units.zh: 洪州監軍高重昌誣奏信州刺史李位謀大逆，追赴京師。
units.en: Hongzhou army supervisor Gao Chongchang falsely reported that Xin Prefecture governor Li Wei was plotting treason. Li was summoned to the capital.
units.literal: Hongzhou army supervisor Gao Chongchang falsely memorialized that Xin Prefecture governor Li Wei plotted great treason; Li was summoned to the capital.

units.zh: 存誠一日三表，請付位於御史臺。
units.en: Cuncheng submitted three memorials in a single day, asking that Li Wei be turned over to the Censorate.
units.literal: Cuncheng submitted three memorials in one day, requesting that Li Wei be entrusted to the Censorate.

units.zh: 及推案無狀，位竟得雪。
units.en: When the case was investigated and found baseless, Li Wei was finally cleared.
units.literal: When the case was investigated and no substance was found, Li Wei was finally cleared.

units.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。
units.en: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。
units.en: After Cui Yin's execution, Shu's ties to Quanzhong kept him in the chancellorship unchanged.
units.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because of his longstanding closeness to Quanzhong Shu's chancellorship remained unchanged.

units.zh: 其年冬，昭宗幸華州，崔胤貶官，樞亦為工部尚書。
units.en: That winter Zhaozong went to Huazhou; Yin was demoted and Shu was made minister of works.
units.literal: That winter Zhaozong went to Huazhou; Yin was demoted and Shu was made Minister of Works.

units.zh: 及李逢吉殲朋黨以專政柄，而顗附麗之跡尤密，頗為時人所譏。
units.en: When Li Fengji destroyed the factions to monopolize power, Yan clung to him more closely than ever and was widely criticized.
units.literal: When Li Fengji destroyed factional groups to monopolize power, Yan's traces of attachment to him were especially close, and he was much ridiculed by men of the time.

units.zh: 太子少保韋倫、太府卿張獻恭等奏：「袁高所奏至當，高是陛下一良臣，望加優異。」
units.en: Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent Wei Lun, Minister of the Imperial Treasury Zhang Xiangong, and others submitted, 'Yuan Gao's memorial was entirely right. Gao is a good minister of Your Majesty. I hope he may receive special favor.'
units.literal: Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent Wei Lun, Minister of the Imperial Treasury Zhang Xiangong, and others submitted: 'Yuan Gao's memorial was entirely appropriate; Gao is a good minister of Your Majesty—I hope he may receive special favor.'

units.zh: 貞元元年，德宗復用吉州長史盧杞為饒州刺史，令高草詔書。
units.en: In Zhenyuan 1 Dezong again appointed Lu Qi, former senior administrator of Jizhou, prefect of Raozhou and ordered Gao to draft the edict.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, Dezong again employed Lu Qi, senior administrator of Jizhou, as prefect of Raozhou and ordered Gao to draft the edict.

units.zh: 伏願陛下哀忠念舊，愛孤恤寡，矜愚嘉善，舍過記功，敦骨肉之情，廣寬仁之路，思堯、舜之風，慕禹、湯之德，克己復禮，以成美化，天下幸甚。」
units.en: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."
units.literal: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual, to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."

units.zh: 復出，宰相李勉、盧翰、劉從一方同歸中書，中使馬欽緒至，揖從一，附耳語而退，諸相各歸閣。
units.en: Fu went out. Chief ministers Li Mian, Lu Han, and Liu Congyi together returned to the Secretariat. Palace envoy Ma Qinxu arrived, bowed to Liu Congyi, whispered in his ear, and withdrew. The ministers each returned to their offices.
units.literal: Fu went out; chief ministers Li Mian, Lu Han, and Liu Congyi together returned to the Secretariat; palace envoy Ma Qinxu arrived, bowed to Congyi, whispered in his ear, and withdrew; the ministers each returned to their offices.

units.zh: 今勉、翰不可在相位，即去之；
units.en: If Li Mian and Lu Han ought not be in chief minister posts, then remove them;
units.literal: If Mian and Han ought not be in chief minister posts, then remove them;

units.zh: 從一詣復曰：「適欽緒宣旨，令與公商量朝來所奏便進，勿令李勉、盧翰知。」
units.en: Liu Congyi went to Fu and said, "Just now Qinxu announced the imperial intent, ordering me to consult with you and immediately advance this morning's memorial. Do not let Li Mian and Lu Han know."
units.literal: Congyi went to Fu and said: 'Just now Qinxu announced the imperial intent, ordering me to consult with you and immediately advance this morning's memorial; do not let Li Mian and Lu Han know.'

units.zh: 元載以罪誅，除揆睦州刺史，入拜國子祭酒、禮部尚書，為盧杞所惡。
units.en: After Yuan Zai was executed for his crimes, Kui was appointed prefect of Muzhou. He later entered court as Director of the Directorate of Education and Minister of Rites, but Lu Qi bore him ill will.
units.literal: When Yuan Zai was executed for crime, Kui was appointed prefect of Muzhou; he entered court as Director of the Directorate of Education and Minister of Rites, but was hated by Lu Qi.

units.zh: 唐興，因隋樂不改，及黃巢之亂，樂縣散失，太常博士殷盈孫以周法鑄穀鐘、編鐘，處士蕭承訓等校石磐，合而奏之。
units.en: When the Tang rose, they retained Sui music unchanged. During Huang Chao's rebellion the court instruments were scattered and lost. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun recast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, while the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others retuned stone chimes, and the restored ensemble was played together once more.
units.literal: When the Tang rose, they took over Sui music without change; at the turmoil of Huang Chao the musical stands were scattered and lost; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun cast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, and the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others tuned stone chimes, and together they were played.

units.zh: 劉晏，字士安，曹州南華人。
units.en: Liu Yan, styled Shi'an, came from Nanhua in Caozhou.
units.literal: Liu Yan, courtesy name Shi'an, was a native of Nanhua in Caozhou.

units.zh: 時顏真卿以文學正直出為利州刺史，晏舉真卿自代為戶部，乃加國子祭酒。
units.en: When Yan Zhenqing, admired for scholarship and integrity, had been posted to Lizhou, Liu Yan proposed that Zhenqing succeed him at the Ministry of Revenue and was himself made chancellor of the national university in addition.
units.literal: At that time Yan Zhenqing, known for literary learning and uprightness, had been sent out as prefect of Lizhou; Yan recommended Zhenqing to succeed him in the Revenue Ministry, and Yan was additionally made Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

units.zh: 年七歲，舉神童，授秘書省正字。
units.en: At seven he was nominated as a precocious youth and made Regular Scribe in the Secretariat.
units.literal: At age seven he was recommended as a child prodigy and appointed Regular Scribe of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 歷殿中侍御史，遷度支郎中、杭隴華三州刺史，尋遷河南尹。
units.en: He held the post of palace attendant censor, then rose to vice director of the revenue bureau and prefect of Hang, Long, and Hua, and shortly afterward became Intendant of the Henan circuit.
units.literal: He served as Attendant Censor in the Palace, was promoted to Vice Director in the Bureau of Revenue, and became prefect of Hang, Long, and Hua; soon after he was transferred to Intendant of Henan.

units.zh: 寶應二年，遷吏部尚書、平章事，領度支鹽鐵轉運租庸使。
units.en: In 763 he became minister of civil appointments and chief minister, continuing to head the combined revenue, salt, iron, transport, and corvée administration.
units.literal: In the second year of Baoying he was transferred to Minister of Personnel and made Grand Councilor, while retaining his posts as Commissioner for Revenue, Salt, Iron, Transport, and the Corvée Tax.

units.zh: 累授夏縣令，有能名。
units.en: Through successive appointments he became magistrate of Xia County and became known for administrative ability.
units.literal: He was repeatedly appointed magistrate of Xia County and gained a reputation for competence.

units.zh: 晏受命後，以轉運為己任，凡所經歷，必究利病之由。
units.en: Once charged with the task, Yan treated grain transport as his own mission and wherever he went traced every cause of waste or efficiency.
units.literal: After Yan received his mandate, he made transport his personal responsibility, and wherever he traveled he thoroughly investigated the causes of profit and harm.

units.zh: 時史朝義盜據東都，寄理長水。
units.en: With Shi Chaoyi holding the Eastern Capital, Yan governed from Changshui as his provisional seat.
units.literal: At that time Shi Chaoyi was occupying the Eastern Capital by force, so he administered affairs from Changshui.

units.zh: 入為京兆尹，頃之，加戶部侍郎、兼御史中丞，判度支，委府事於司錄張群、杜亞，綜大體，議論號為稱職。
units.en: Recalled to serve as metropolitan governor of Chang'an, he soon added the titles of vice minister of revenue and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, with charge of the revenue bureau. He left routine office work to Zhang Qun and Du Ya as recorders while he kept the broad direction in hand, and contemporaries judged his policy judgments sound.
units.literal: He entered the capital as Metropolitan Governor; shortly thereafter he was additionally appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and Concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, with charge of revenue; he entrusted administrative affairs to Clerks Zhang Qun and Du Ya, while he handled overall policy, and his deliberations were said to be competent.

units.zh: 復入為京兆尹、戶部侍郎，判度支。
units.en: He returned to Chang'an as metropolitan governor and vice minister of revenue, again supervising the revenue bureau.
units.literal: He was recalled to serve again as Metropolitan Governor and Vice Minister of Revenue, with charge of revenue.

units.zh: 無何，為酷吏敬羽所構，貶通州刺史。
units.en: Not long after, the notorious official Jing Yu engineered charges against him, and he was demoted to prefect of Tongzhou.
units.literal: Before long he was framed by the harsh official Jing Yu and demoted to prefect of Tongzhou.

units.zh: 坐與中官程元振交通，元振得罪，晏罷相，為太子賓客。
units.en: Charged with ties to the eunuch Cheng Yuanzhen, he lost the premiership when Yuanzhen was disgraced and was appointed mentor to the crown prince.
units.literal: He was punished for associating with the eunuch Cheng Yuanzhen; when Yuanzhen fell from power, Yan was removed from the chancellorship and made Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 尋授御史大夫，領東都、河南、江淮、山南等道轉運租庸鹽鐵使如故。
units.en: He was soon made Censor-in-Chief while retaining his former commissions for transport, zu-yong taxes, salt, and iron over the Eastern Capital, Henan, Jianghuai, Shannan, and related circuits.
units.literal: Soon after he was appointed Censor-in-Chief and continued to hold his former posts as Transport Commissioner for the Eastern Capital, Henan, Jianghuai, Shan'nan, and other circuits, as well as Commissioner for the Corvée Tax, Salt, and Iron.

units.zh: 至江淮，以書遺元載曰：
units.en: Reaching Jianghuai, he wrote Yuan Zai:
units.literal: When he reached the Jianghuai region, he sent a letter to Yuan Zai saying:

units.zh: 浮於淮、泗，達於汴，入於河，西循底柱、硤石、少華，楚帆越客，直抵建章、長樂，此安社稷之奇策也。
units.en: Grain could float up the Huai and Si, reach Bian, enter the Yellow River, and run west past Dizhu, Xiaoshi, and Shaohua so that Chu and Yue shipping would berth straight at the imperial palaces—this was the bold plan to stabilize the dynasty.
units.literal: Floating on the Huai and Si, reaching Bian, entering the Yellow River, and proceeding west along Dizhu, Xiaoshi, and Shaohua—Chu sails and Yue merchants arriving straight at Jianzhang and Changle: this is the extraordinary stratagem to secure the state.

units.zh: 晏賓於東朝，猶有官謗，相公終始故舊，不信流言，賈誼復召宣室，弘羊重興功利，敢不悉力以答所知。
units.en: Though as a guest at the Eastern Court I still face official slander, you have remained my old friend from first to last and will not heed idle talk. Just as Jia Yi was called back to the privy chamber and Sang Hongyang was trusted again to manage state revenue, I dare not spare myself in repaying your confidence.
units.literal: Yan, though favored at the Eastern Court, still bore official slander; the Chancellor had been my friend from first to last—do not believe wandering rumors; Jia Yi was summoned again to the Xuan Chamber, and Sang Hongyang revived profit and utility—how dare I not exert every effort to repay one who knows me?

units.zh: 驅馬陜郊，見三門渠津遺跡。
units.en: Traveling through the lands west of Shan, I found the remains of the Sanmen canal works.
units.literal: Riding through the Shaan suburbs, I saw the vestiges of the canals and crossings at Sanmen.

units.zh: 到河陰、鞏、洛，見宇文愷置梁公堰，分黃河水入通濟渠；
units.en: At Heyin, Gong, and Luoyang I inspected Yuwen Kai's weir diverting Yellow River water into the Tongji Canal;
units.literal: At Heyin, Gong, and Luo I saw how Yuwen Kai had built the Duke of Liang's weir to divide the Yellow River into the Tongji Canal;

units.zh: 大夫李傑新堤故事，飾像河廟，凜然如生。
units.en: and Li Jie's later embankment, with life-like images set up at the River God shrine.
units.literal: and the story of Censor-in-Chief Li Jie's new embankment, with statues adorned at the River Temple, stern as though living.

units.zh: 涉滎郊、浚澤，遙瞻淮甸，步步探討，知昔人用心，則潭、衡、桂陽必多積谷，關輔汲汲，只緣兵糧。
units.en: Passing through the Song riverland and dredging the marshes, scanning the Huai plain at every turn, I saw why the ancients labored as they did: the lake districts around Tan, Heng, and Guiyang must hold huge reserves, while Guanzhong starves chiefly for want of army rations.
units.literal: Crossing the Song suburbs and dredging marshes, gazing from afar at the Huai district, investigating step by step—I knew how our predecessors applied their minds: Tan, Heng, and Guiyang surely store abundant grain; the Guanzhong region strains only because of military grain.

units.zh: 漕引瀟、湘、洞庭，萬里幾日，淪波卦席，西指長安。
units.en: Once grain is floated down the Xiao, the Xiang, and Dongting Lake, ten thousand li can be covered in days, with sails quartering the waves all the way west to Chang'an.
units.literal: Transport by water from the Xiao and Xiang and Dongting—in a few days over ten thousand li—the waves rolling like mat patterns on deck, pointing west to Chang'an.

units.zh: 三秦之人，待此而飽；
units.en: The people of the Three Qin regions would at last eat their fill;
units.literal: The people of the Three Qins will rely on this to be fed;

units.zh: 六軍之眾，待此而強。
units.en: the imperial armies would grow strong on it.
units.literal: the masses of the Six Armies will rely on this to be strengthened.

units.zh: 天子無側席之憂，都人見泛舟之役；
units.en: The emperor would no longer fret from hunger, and the capital would see grain boats plying the canals again;
units.literal: The Son of Heaven will have no worry of sitting sideways on his mat; the capital populace will see boats passing to and fro;

units.zh: 四方旅拒者可以破膽，三河流離者於茲請命。
units.en: rebels in the provinces would lose heart, and refugees along the Yellow, Huai, and other rivers could beg for relief.
units.literal: those who resist from the four quarters can have their courage broken; those displaced along the Three Rivers can here plead for their lives.

units.zh: 相公匡戴明主，為富人侯，此今之切務，不可失也。
units.en: By supporting our enlightened sovereign you would become a great lord of wealth—this is the urgent task of the moment and must not be let slip.
units.literal: The Chancellor aids and supports the enlightened sovereign and becomes a marquis among wealthy men—this is today's urgent task and must not be missed.

units.zh: 使仆湔洗瑕穢，率罄愚懦，當憑經義，請護河堤，冥勤在官，不辭水死。
units.en: Give me leave to clear my name and give all my poor wits to the cause. On principle I ask to defend the river works myself, to labor at my post in silence, and not to shirk death by drowning.
units.literal: Enable this servant to wash away stains, lead with all my foolish timidity, rely on canonical principles, request to guard the river dikes, labor in office in obscurity, and not refuse death by water.

units.zh: 然運之利病，各有四五焉。
units.en: Yet transport has its own four or five advantages and as many drawbacks.
units.literal: Yet the profit and harm of transport each have four or five aspects.

units.zh: 晏自尹京入為計相，共五年矣。
units.en: I have been metropolitan governor and then chief fiscal officer for five years altogether.
units.literal: Yan, from governing the capital to becoming chief of finance, has served five years in all.

units.zh: 京師三輔百姓，唯苦稅畝傷多，若使江、湖米來每年三二十萬，即頓減徭賦，歌舞皇澤，其利一也。
units.en: The people around Chang'an groan under heavy land taxes; if two or three hundred thousand piculs of Jianghu grain arrived yearly, levies could drop at once and they would praise the throne's bounty—that is the first gain.
units.literal: The people of the capital and the Three Adjuncts suffer only from excessive land tax; if two or three hundred thousand piculs of grain from the rivers and lakes came each year, corvée and levies would be sharply reduced and they would sing of the sovereign's grace—this is the first benefit.

units.zh: 東都殘毀，百無一存。
units.en: The Eastern Capital is in ruins; scarcely one building in a hundred still stands.
units.literal: The Eastern Capital lies in ruins; not one part in a hundred remains.

units.zh: 若米運流通，則饑人皆附，村落邑厘，從此滋多。
units.en: If grain shipping revives, starving refugees will settle there and hamlets will spring up again.
units.literal: If grain transport flows freely, the hungry will all gather, and villages and hamlets will multiply from this.

units.zh: 受命之日引海陵之倉以食鞏、洛，是計之得者，其利二也。
units.en: From the day I took office I have drawn Hailing's stores to feed Gong and Luoyang—a sound plan and the second gain.
units.literal: From the day of my mandate I have drawn on the granaries of Hailing to feed Gong and Luo—this is a sound plan; that is the second benefit.

units.zh: 諸將有在邊者，諸戎有侵敗王略者，或聞三江、五湖，貢輸紅粒，雲帆桂楫，輸納帝鄉，軍誌曰：「先聲後實，可以震耀夷夏。」
units.en: Frontier generals and tribes that raid the borders, hearing that red grain from the Yangzi lakes is shipped on cloud-white sails and cassia-prowed boats to the capital, will recall the maxim that reputation should precede force—thus aweing both barbarian and Chinese.'
units.literal: Generals stationed on the frontier and barbarians who encroach on the imperial domain—when they hear that from the Three Rivers and Five Lakes red grain is presented in tribute, with cloudlike sails and cassia oars shipping it to the imperial capital, military doctrine says: 'Sound precedes substance; this can awe barbarians and Chinese alike.'

units.zh: 其利三也。
units.en: That is the third gain.
units.literal: That is the third benefit.

units.zh: 自古帝王之盛，皆云書同文，車同軌，日月所照，莫不率俾。
units.en: Since antiquity the height of imperial power has been described as one script, one track, and universal submission to the throne.
units.literal: From antiquity the glory of emperors has been described as identical script and identical wheel-gauge, and all beneath the sun and moon submitting in obedience.

units.zh: 今舟車既通，商賈往來，百貨雜集，航海梯山，聖神輝光，漸近貞觀、永徽之盛，其利四也。
units.en: With waterways and roads open again, merchants travel freely, goods pile up, and trade spans sea and mountain—the court's glory would approach the prosperity of the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras; that is the fourth gain.
units.literal: Now that boats and carts are connected, merchants come and go, goods of every kind gather, and trade crosses seas and mountains—the sage sovereign's radiance approaches the splendor of Zhenguan and Yonghui; that is the fourth benefit.

units.zh: 所可疑者，函、陜雕殘，東周尤甚。
units.en: What gives pause is the devastation of Hangu Pass and Shaan, worst of all in the old Eastern Zhou heartland.
units.literal: What gives pause is that Hangu and Shaan are carved to ruin, and the Eastern Zhou region is worst of all.

units.zh: 過宜陽、熊耳，至武牢、成臯，五百里中，編戶千余而已。
units.en: From Yiyang and Xiong'er to Wulao and Chenggao, five hundred li hold barely a thousand registered households.
units.literal: From Yiyang and Xiong'er to Wulao and Chenggao, within five hundred li there are only a little over a thousand registered households.

units.zh: 居無尺椽，人無煙爨，蕭條淒慘，獸遊鬼哭。
units.en: Not a rafter stands, no hearth smoke rises; the land is desolate, beasts roam, and it seems ghosts wail.
units.literal: Homes lack a single rafter; people lack cooking smoke; desolation is bleak and beasts roam while ghosts seem to wail.

units.zh: 牛必羸角，輿必說輹，棧車輓漕，亦不易求。
units.en: Oxen are emaciated, cart wheels fall off, and even simple haulage carts are hard to find.
units.literal: Oxen are sure to be scrawny-horned, carts sure to have wheels come loose; even plank carts for haulage are not easily found.

units.zh: 今於無人之境，興此勞人之運，固難就矣，其病一也。
units.en: To launch this laborious transport through uninhabited country is bound to fail—that is the first drawback.
units.literal: To launch this labor-consuming transport in a land without people is inherently hard to accomplish—that is the first drawback.

units.zh: 河、汴有初，不修則毀澱，故每年正月發近縣丁男，塞長茭，決沮淤，清明桃花已後，遠水自然安流，陽侯、宓妃，不復太息。
units.en: The Yellow River and Bian Canal must be dredged yearly or they silt shut; each New Year laborers from nearby counties clear reeds and sediment, and after Qingming the distant reaches run clear again without the river gods' lament.
units.literal: The Yellow River and Bian Canal had their beginnings; if not maintained they silt up, so every first month conscript labor from nearby counties blocks long reeds and clears sediment; after Qingming and the peach blossoms, distant waters flow smoothly of themselves, and the River Lord and Lady Mi need sigh no more.

units.zh: 頃因寇難，總不掏拓，澤滅水，岸石崩，役夫需於沙，津吏旋於濘，千里洄上，罔水舟行，其病二也。
units.en: Since the rebellions dredging has stopped entirely; marshes have swallowed the channel, banks have collapsed, laborers wait on sandbars, clerks flounder in mud, and for a thousand li upstream boats cannot sail—that is the second drawback.
units.literal: Recently because of rebellion dredging has altogether ceased; marshes have swallowed the water, bank stones have collapsed, laborers wait on sandbars, ferry clerks turn in the mud, and for a thousand li upstream there is no water for boats—that is the second drawback.

units.zh: 東垣、底柱，澠池、二陵，北河運處五六百里，戍卒久絕，縣吏空拳。
units.en: From Dongyuan and Dizhu to Mianchi and the Two Mounds, five or six hundred li of the northern transport route have no garrisons left and county officials are powerless.
units.literal: From Dongyuan and Dizhu to Mianchi and the Two Mounds, five or six hundred li along the northern river transport route—garrison troops have long been cut off and county clerks are empty-handed.

units.zh: 奪攘奸宄，窟穴囊橐。
units.en: Bandits and outlaws raid and hide in caves with their plunder.
units.literal: Robbers and villains plunder and nest in caves with their loot.

units.zh: 夾河為藪，豺狼狺狺，舟行所經，寇亦能往，其病三也。
units.en: Marshes line the river, wolves howl, and wherever boats can go bandits can follow—that is the third drawback.
units.literal: Along the river are marshes; wolves and jackals snarl; wherever boats pass, bandits can also go—that is the third drawback.

units.zh: 東自淮陰，西臨蒲阪，亙三千里，屯戍相望。
units.en: From Huaiyin in the east to Pufan in the west, three thousand li of garrisons stand face to face.
units.literal: From Huaiyin in the east to Pufan in the west, spanning three thousand li, garrisons face one another.

units.zh: 中軍皆鼎司元侯，賤卒儀同青紫，每雲食半菽，又雲無挾纊，輓漕所至，船到便留，即非單車使折簡書所能制矣，其病四也。
units.en: Central Army posts are held by chief ministers and great lords; common soldiers dress like officers; they claim to eat half rations and lack winter coats; wherever grain convoys arrive the boats are seized on the spot—not something a lone commissioner with a letter can restrain—that is the fourth drawback.
units.literal: Central Army posts are held by chief ministers and great marquises; lowly soldiers dress like the purple-clad elite; they always say they eat half beans and have no padded coats; wherever transport grain arrives, boats are detained on arrival—this is not something a lone envoy with a letter can control; that is the fourth drawback.

units.zh: 惟小子畢其慮奔走之，惟中書詳其利病裁成之。
units.en: I alone will give all my thought and effort to the task; only the Secretariat can weigh the pros and cons and bring the plan to completion.
units.literal: Only this humble servant will exhaust his thought and run about it; only the Secretariat will weigh profit and harm and complete the plan.

units.zh: 晏累年已來，事缺名毀，聖慈含育，特賜生全。
units.en: For years my duties were curtailed and my name slandered; the emperor's mercy spared my life.
units.literal: Yan for many years has had his duties cut short and his name slandered; the sage's compassion nurtured him and specially granted him life.

units.zh: 月余家居，遽即臨遣，恩榮感切，思殞百身。
units.en: After barely a month at home I was suddenly dispatched on imperial business; overwhelmed by grace, I would gladly die a hundred deaths in return.
units.literal: After a month at home he was suddenly sent on imperial mission; moved by grace and honor, he wished to die a hundred deaths in return.

units.zh: 見一水不通，願荷鍤而先往；
units.en: Wherever a channel was blocked I wished to take a spade and go first;
units.literal: seeing one waterway blocked, he wished to shoulder a spade and go first;

units.zh: 見一粒不運，願負米而先趨。
units.en: wherever a grain was not moved I wished to carry rice and hurry ahead.
units.literal: seeing one grain not transported, he wished to carry rice and hurry ahead.

units.zh: 焦心苦形，期報明主，丹誠未克，漕引多虞，屏營中流，掩泣獻狀。
units.en: I wore myself out in body and mind to repay my sovereign; my loyal effort had not yet succeeded and transport still faced many perils; pacing midstream in anxiety, I wept as I submitted this memorial.
units.literal: He tormented heart and body, hoping to repay the enlightened sovereign; his red sincerity had not yet succeeded, and grain transport had many worries; pacing anxiously midstream, he wept as he presented his memorial.

units.zh: 自此每歲運米數十萬石以濟關中。
units.en: From then on several hundred thousand piculs of grain were shipped yearly to supply Guanzhong.
units.literal: From this time each year several hundred thousand piculs of grain were transported to relieve Guanzhong.

units.zh: 十一月，安祿山據范陽叛。
units.en: In the eleventh month An Lushan rebelled from Fanyang.
units.literal: In the eleventh month An Lushan seized Fanyang and rebelled.

units.zh: 十三日，祿山陷東京，常清以餘眾奔陜州，謂仙芝曰：「累日血戰，賊鋒不可當。
units.en: On the thirteenth Lushan took the Eastern Capital; Changqing fled with his survivors to Shanzhou and told Xianzhi, "We have fought for days in blood — the rebel host cannot be stopped.
units.literal: On the thirteenth Lushan took the Eastern Capital; Changqing fled with his remaining troops to Shanzhou and said to Xianzhi: "For days we have fought in blood; the rebels' spearhead cannot be withstood.

units.zh: 趙彥深嘗謂耀曰：「君研尋《左氏》，豈求服虔、杜預之紕繆邪？」
units.en: Zhao Yanshen once said to Yao, "In studying the Zuo Tradition, are you trying to find errors in Fu Qian and Du Yu?"
units.literal: Zhao Yanshen once said to Yao, "When you study and search the Zuo Tradition, are you seeking the errors of Fu Qian and Du Yu?"

units.zh: 貞元十五年，代李復為鄭滑節度使。
units.en: In Zhenyuan 15 he replaced Li Fu as military commissioner of Zheng-Hua.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan he replaced Li Fu as military commissioner of Zheng-Hua.
